To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

training paradigms, technology acceptance constructs, and their relationships are important factors in understanding and improving the effectiveness of training programs and the use of information technologies.

the UTAUT constructs are applicable to the training domain and that training reaction is an important construct in the technology acceptance domain, and that the relationship between the training paradigma and the technology acceptance construct is partially mediated through training reactions.

training paradigms have a significant impact on technology acceptance constructs and that technology acceptance constructs have a significant impact, mediated by training reactions, on behavioral intentions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of training paradigms on the UTAUT constructs, and the impact of the UTAUT on training outcomes.
the impact of training in the context of technology acceptance, and the results provide a basis for the design, implementation, and evaluation of technology acceptance models.
the impact of training on technology acceptance and its impact on the technology acceptance constructs as reflected in the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the training paradigm is an important factor in technology acceptance and that training paradigms are a key factor in determining the success of technology acceptance.

the proposed framework is a valid representation of the relationships between training reactions, technology acceptance, and behavioral intention to adopt and use information technology in the context of training programs.
training reactions have a direct effect on behavioral intention to use and a partial mediating effect on behavioral intention through facilitating conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

training paradigms, such as instructional systems design, cognitive learning theory, and andragogy, can help to explain the technology acceptance constructs, and that training reactions, such as perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, can be used to predict the behavioral intention to use technology.
the training reaction constructs have a positive relationship with the behavioral intention construct.
the technology acceptance constructs as reflected in the Unified Theory are applicable to training programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
training reactions can serve as a useful predictor of behavioral intentions to use.
training reactions and behavioral intent to use are significantly related.
the technology acceptance constructs are relevant to training and that training paradigms are relevant to technology acceptance.
